text.p: BHF Bank said on Thursday that it had downgraded Bayerische Hypotheken und Wechselbank and reduced its earnings estimates after the bank on Wednesday released its results, indicating a capital rise was needed.

"We cut our recommendation to sell from buy and moved our 1997 earnings per share estimate to 2.70 marks from 3.10 marks, the 1998 to 3.40 marks from 3.60 marks," BHF Bank analyst Dieter Hein told Reuters.
The main reason for the downgrade was that Hypo-Bank would likely need to raise capital, Hein said, adding: "The bank needs to raise capital and I think they will do it this year."
Hein explained that the Hypo-Bank equity to assets ratio was dangerously low that a capital rise could be needed relatively soon.
Hein also stressed that Hypo-Bank's operating profit for 1996 had dropped nine percent while rival banks' performance was significantly stronger.
Hypo-Bank also earmarked a significantly higher amount of funds for reserves than other banks had done, but failed to explain the reason for this move; a very worrying sign Hein said.
While Hypo-Bank is the smallest of Germany's largest commercial banks it has the highest risk provision, a fact that is very puzzling to analysts.
"They have much higher risk provisions than the others which they did not explain however leading to the presumption that they may have...problems in their credit portfolio," Hein said.
Hypo-Bank's shares fell 3.52 percent to 53.45 marks while the broader DAX index was down only 0.07 percent at 3,357.17 points.
